subject.title: fix(sqlite): stop mount probes blocking database startup

question: Should SQLite database opening ever synchronously execute the system `mount` command, or must an unclassifiable path immediately use rollback journaling without starting a subprocess?
rationale: A timeout cannot make Node's synchronous subprocess call a hard deadline, while removing the probe may conservatively disable WAL for some local macOS/BSD paths; choosing that availability-versus-performance boundary requires owner intent.

options.title: Remove the startup subprocess
options.body: Treat unavailable filesystem classification as unsafe for WAL and continue immediately with rollback journaling.

options.title: Preclassify outside database opening
options.body: Move mount discovery to an asynchronously bounded lifecycle owner and pass the prepared classification into synchronous database setup.

options.title: Accept the residual stall risk
options.body: Keep the synchronous timeout only with explicit owner acceptance and supported-host proof documenting that it is best-effort rather than a hard deadline.

recommendation.title: Remove the startup subprocess
recommendation.body: Treat unavailable filesystem classification as unsafe for WAL and continue immediately with rollback journaling.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned to the PR and authored most current-head refinements, making them the clearest available owner for the startup-boundary decision.
